title: Zhangjiajie on a budget - total cost
text: Zhangjiajie is among the most affordable top parks in the world. A realistic 4-day budget: accommodation 400-800 yuan, tickets 770 yuan, food 200-300 yuan, transport 100 yuan - about 1,500-2,000 yuan total. Hostels start at 40 yuan, solid 3-star hotels from 200 yuan.

title: Zhangjiajie for seniors - accessible routes
text: The park is more accessible than it looks thanks to elevators, cable cars and buses. Best routes: upper plateau via Bailong Elevator (flat paths between viewpoints), the first 2-3 km of Golden Whip Stream, and Tianmen with cable car plus escalator instead of 999 steps.

title: Zhangjiajie with kids - what to consider
text: The park suits families well but needs planning. Under 3: use a baby carrier (strollers useless on stairs). Ages 4-7: Golden Whip Stream is ideal - flat, wet, full of bridges and monkeys. Ages 8+: most routes work. Children under 1.2 m enter free.

title: Tea in Zhangjiajie - what to try
text: Hunan is one of China's top tea regions. Local specialties: Mao Jian (delicate green tea from high-altitude buds), Moyao Cha (sweet caffeine-free vine tea used as medicine), and Hei Cha (dark pressed brick tea that ages for decades). Most shops offer free tastings.

title: What to bring home from Zhangjiajie
text: Unique local finds: Tujia sicin brocade (scarves from 50 yuan), polished quartzite sandstone stones from the park, and Mao Jian green tea grown in the mountains. Good gifts include Miao silver jewelry and embroidery. Skip fake jade, cheap magnets and suspicious medicines.
